newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower- dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 lower- dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by further declines in wholesale pork prices, cash hog dealers said.
The weak pork values kept packer operating margins in negative territory, resulting in lower bids for live hogs, sources said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to interior Iowa/southern Minnesota plants could range from $53.00 to $54.00 and Illinois top prices at the plant could range $52.50 to $53.00. Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could span $52.00 to $53.50.
Some packer buyers said they were surprised by the failure of reduced hog slaughter this week to rejuvenate pork prices as supplies dwindled.
Fresh ham prices at midday were quoted by USDA steady to $2.00 per cwt lower, pork bellies were steady and lean trimmings were down $3.00 to $4.00.

Hog slaughter Thursday was estimated at 340,000 head, below 349,000 a week ago and 351,000 a year ago, USDA said. Week to date slaughter was pegged 1.298 million head, down 2.8 percent from a week ago and down 4.7 percent from a year ago.
